cramer.py.summary: Compress or decompress files with snappy, lz4 or gzip through cramjam.
details: Takes a file or a folder, compresses every match (or decompresses the ``.sz``/``.lz4``/``.gz`` files again) with the chosen algorithm, guessing the algorithm from the extension when decompressing. ``--keep`` preserves the originals and ``--skip-existing`` avoids overwriting earlier output.

create_monthly_branch.py.summary: Create and push a ``<month>_<year>`` branch in ``~/bin``.
details: Builds the branch name from the current month, checks whether it exists locally or on the remote, and otherwise fetches, updates ``main``, branches off it and pushes the new branch with upstream tracking before switching back to ``main``.
create_monthly_branch.py.notes: The repository path (``~/bin``) and base branch (``main``) are module constants; edit them for other layouts.

create_stub.py.summary: Generate ``.pyi`` stub files for Python modules with ``stubgen``.
details: Runs ``stubgen`` on the files named on the command line, or on every ``.py`` file below the current directory, skipping modules whose stub already exists and summarising the files that still have no stub.

csv2json.py.summary: Convert a two-column CSV into a JSON object keyed by the first column.
details: The first row is treated as the header; every following row becomes ``{first column: second column}`` and the mapping is written next to the input as ``<name>.json`` with indentation.

csv2json2.py.summary: Convert a CSV file into a JSON list of row objects.
details: Uses :class:`csv.DictReader`, so the header row becomes the keys of each object, and writes the list to ``<name>.json`` with two-space indentation.

csvtojson.py.summary: Convert a CSV file into a JSON list of row objects.
details: Reads the CSV with :class:`csv.DictReader` and writes ``<name>.json`` next to the input, indented by four spaces.

csym.py.summary: Create extension-less symlinks for the scripts in the personal bin folders.
details: For ``~/bashbin`` (``.sh``) and ``~/bin`` plus ``~/.local/bin`` (``.py``) it adds a symlink without the extension pointing at the script, so the tools can be called by name. Existing non-symlink entries with the same name are replaced.

cwin.py.summary: Delete macOS and Windows clutter files from a directory tree.
details: Matches the usual artefacts (``.DS_Store``, ``._*``, ``.Trashes``, ``Thumbs.db``, ``desktop.ini``, ``*.exe``, ``*.dll``, ``*.lnk`` ...) while walking the given paths, and removes them or lists them in dry-run mode.

cytonizer.py.summary: Run ``cythonize`` over Cython sources in parallel.
details: Collects the ``.pyx`` files given on the command line (directories are searched recursively) or below the current directory and runs ``cythonize`` in each file's parent directory with a worker pool.

dcode.py.summary: Peel encoded strings recursively and rank the plausible plain-text results.
details: Applies base64, base32, base16, base58, hex, URL, ROT13/ROT47, Atbash, binary, HTML-entity, unicode-escape, gzip/zlib/bz2/lzma, and single-byte XOR decoders in a bounded search tree, scores each candidate by English letter frequency and prints the most readable chains (optionally as JSON).

decode_phonetic.py.summary: Unescape HTML entities in a file in place.
details: Reads the file, applies :func:`html.unescape` and writes the result back, replacing ``&``, ``é`` and similar entities with the characters they stand for.

decode_unicode.py.summary: Convert a text file to plain ASCII by stripping the accents.
details: Normalizes the text to NFKD and encodes it as ASCII while ignoring the characters that cannot be represented, so ``café`` becomes ``cafe``. The file is rewritten in place.

decryptor.py.summary: Encrypt or decrypt every file in the current directory with AES-CBC.
details: ``--encrypt`` generates a random 32-character key, prints it and prepends a fresh IV to each encrypted file; ``--decrypt`` needs the same key via ``--key``. PKCS7 padding is applied and the files are overwritten in place, the running script itself being skipped.

deduptools.py.summary: Find and remove duplicate definitions with regexes, ASTs or tree-sitter.
details: The ``const`` subcommand drops repeated constant assignments in one file, ``ast`` hashes (normalised) top-level functions, classes and constants across the given paths and writes one representative per duplicate to ``utils.py``, ``ts`` does the same by tree-sitter source text, and ``refactor`` extracts the surviving definitions into a package. ``--exclude``/``--exclude-self`` filter the inputs.
